title: Quicksort's worst case hides in already-sorted input
body: Quicksort is fast on average because pivots usually split work evenly. Pick the first element as pivot on sorted data and every split is maximally lopsided, degrading to n-squared. Random or median pivots do not remove the worst case, they make it vanishingly unlikely to stumble into.
source_hint: Hoare 1962; CLRS analysis of randomised quicksort
